utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Good afternoon. Mr. Registrar, have the accused brought in, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Let me say hello to the interpreters. This is also a way of checking whether everyone is ready. I hope everyone had a nice weekend. I, of course, say good afternoon to the Prosecution and to the Defence. We are ready to continue with our witness and his examination-in-chief, which has not been completed. You will remind me of his name, General Slavko ...

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Slavko Marin.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Nobilo. I think that the witness may be brought in.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: General, can you hear me?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Very well. We are going to continue with the examination-in-chief by Defence counsel for the accused, Mr. Nobilo. I remind you that you are still under oath.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Brigadier. Today, we should like to begin with a reconstruction of the events of the April war, at least the key ten days of that period which are covered by the indictment. Before that, I should like to hear your opinion. You're an officer of the Army of the Federation. Can you now, from this time distance, explain to us what you think was the cause of the conflict between the Croats and the Muslims in Central Bosnia, in the first place, where you were working at the time?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN
utterances.text: Mr. President, Your Honours, the causes of the conflict between the Croats and Muslims or Bosniaks in Bosnia and, therefore, in Central Bosnia as well, in my personal opinion, are multi-fold. On this occasion, I should like to highlight only a few. The first cause of the conflict, which I should like to point to, is a concept of defence that differed from that of the former JNA and the initial wavering on the part of the Muslims during the aggression against Bosnia-Herzegovina. I have repeated several times the statement by a member of the presidency of Bosnia-Herzegovina, that is, Mr. Alija Izetbegovic. Following the aggression on the village of Ravno, he said, "This is not our war." Such an approach among the Croats in Bosnia-Herzegovina caused a distrust with regard to the Territorial Defence of the time and certain reservations with respect to whether the Muslims would participate in the defence of the sovereignty of Bosnia-Herzegovina. I shall try to recall and indicate only a few of the places which were attacked at the beginning of 1992 and which the HVO, suffering considerable casualties, managed to halt the aggression by the army of Republika Srpska. Among those places are Kupres, Ravno, Livno, Novi Travnik, Jajce, Travnik, Zepce and, in eastern Herzegovina, the Neretva River Valley where the HVO actually took upon itself the initial blow, the initial strike. What else was happening at that time? In the parts of northwestern Bosnia and the localities of Petrovac, Kluce, Krupa, Sanski Most, Donji Vakuf, and other places, the Muslims/Bosniaks represented a relative majority of the population, and the Croats, an absolute minority. Where the HVO was not organised, those places fell under the control of the army of Republika Srpska within a day or two, and the entire population was expelled from those places, including women, children, old people, and soldiers. In view of these facts, it was natural that the people that were suffering casualties set up its defences against the army of Republika Srpska and developed a certain degree of mistrust. Another element that I consider to be important is that, in virtually all the municipalities in Central Bosnia, the positions of commanders of the municipal Territorial Defence were Muslims/Bosniaks. This also applied to the district headquarters of Territorial Defence, in which the commander was also a Muslim. But we had a similar situation at the level of Bosnia-Herzegovina as a whole, where the commander of the republican headquarters was also a Muslim/Bosniak. As a result, the Croats felt suppressed, and the Territorial Defence was the first form of organisation in resisting the onslaught of the army of Republika Srpska. A third reason, in my view, is avoidance to organise the defence from the very moment of the attack by the Serbs and the pushing of the Croats into the frontlines. I have already explained this by what I have said so far. Furthermore, another reason is that Muslims opted for playing the part of the victim and using that part as a form of resistance to present themselves, to the International Community as a victim and wait for the destiny of Bosnia-Herzegovina to be resolved by the International Community, rather than defending it with a force of arms. Another very significant problem that encompassed Central Bosnia was the Bosniak refugees expelled by the Serbs from the municipalities I have mentioned in northwestern Bosnia, which settled in areas with mixed populations and, thereby, upset the delicate balance of interethnic relations. The Croats felt in jeopardy, and there are growing rumours among the population that the Muslims are sufficiently strong to defeat the Croats in Central Bosnia, but for the Serbs, that will have to wait. As a consequence of the large number of displaced persons, among whom were able-bodied men, mobile refugee brigades were set up which would, later on, be used for a struggle for living space. The next reason, in my personal opinion, is the presence of extremists and fundamentalists and the formation of units based on religion. A case in point is the 7th Muslim Brigade, the El Mujahed units, which caused fear and reaction among Croatian extremists. Another reason is that, as a result of the structuring of units on the basis of religion, parts of those units were brought to fringe areas of Muslim villages linked to Croatian villages so as to influence the behaviour of local Muslims and, as a result, intimidate the Croats. Examples of this are Guca Gora, Slimena, Ravno Rostovo (phoen) and Han Bila. Another reason for the conflict between the Croats and Muslims in Central Bosnia is the deployment of the BH army units into the depth of the territory, rather than the frontlines with the Serbs, which upset the balance of forces in space. We saw a map of this on Friday on the easel, from which it was possible to see to what extent HVO forces were engaged on the front against Republika Srpska, whereas the BH army units were deployed within the territory, that is, in villages and areas where there was no front against the Republika Srpska Army. When I say "upsetting the balance of forces in space," I wish to draw attention to a fact that was reality in Bosnia-Herzegovina. In a situation that we found ourselves in, the Croats saw the HVO as their own army; the Serbs, the army of Republika Srpska as their army; and the Muslims/Bosniaks saw the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina as their army. So that the events that followed were linked to this problem, because virtually each people was linked to one of these three mentioned armies. I believe that if we were to go into greater details, we would be able to find other reasons, but I think that these will be sufficient to clear up this point.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Thank you, Brigadier. Let us now move on to some of the events that preceded the 16th of April, that is, the actual armed conflict between the Muslims and Croats in the Lasva Valley.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: May I ask the usher for his assistance to distribute these documents?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: D259, D259A for the English version.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Brigadier, will you please look at this document, its signature and the incoming stamp of the fax? Can you authenticate this document?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN
utterances.text: I recognise the incoming stamp. It was received in the communications centre of the Operative Zone signed by the operations duty officer, Mujo Drago. I know him personally. He was head of the PZO in Nikola Subic-Zrinski, and this document did reach the brigade headquarters.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Was this an example of a routine daily report to the Operative Zone where there were no combat operations?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Could you comment on item 2? Why was this specifically stated, "The Busovaca-Kiseljak road is still not in use"?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN
utterances.text: In a routine daily operative report, if there are no significant events in the area for which the particular unit is responsible, the unit sending the report, then it is customary to point to the basic problem. In this case, it was the fact that Busovaca-Kiseljak was still not open for use.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Thank you. Can we proceed to the next document, please?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: D260, D260A for the English version.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Brigadier, another report, this time dated the 12th of April, that is, four days before the conflict. Can you identify or confirm the authenticity of this report? If so, on what grounds?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN
utterances.text: Yes. That's the incoming stamp from the communications centre. The document was drafted in the Nikola Subic-Zrinksi Brigade. That can be seen from the stamp. Zarko Petrovic is someone I know personally. He was the operations duty officer that night.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: How would you comment on item 4, "New entrenchment of the enemy was observed in the Kula sector, the region from the pool to Krvevine." Who was digging in there?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Just a minor point of clarification, you're asking the witness to authenticate this. In French legal terms, that means to confirm that it is the original. I prefer for him to say that he recognises it, that it is a copy, that, apparently, it is a copy of the original. This is a minor shade of meaning that I should like to draw attention to. Perhaps, one day we will have a real debate in this Tribunal on the nature of originals and on the nature of copies. So I would prefer, instead of asking the witness, "Can you authenticate the document," he can certify that the copy appears to be faithful to the original. Do we agree on that?

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Yes, indeed, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Brigadier, is this an authentic copy of the original document dated 12th April, 1993? If so, how can you tell?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN
utterances.text: Yes. It is an authentic copy. The document was received in the command of the Operative Zone. The stamp is that of the Nikola Subic-Zrinkski Brigade, and the operations duty officer is someone I know personally.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Brigadier, can you tell us what item 4 means? Why was it included in this report and what was it a signal of? Allow me to read it: "New entrenchment of the enemy was observed in the Kula sector, the region from the pool in the direction of Krvevine."

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN
utterances.text: It is clear from item 4 that the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina is undertaking certain measures, certain activities, in this case, digging in in the area of Kula. But why in Kula? Kula is one of the key land features for the defence of Busovaca. That is why this operatives duty officer wanted to underline and draw attention to these activities on the part of the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina. It is also important to point out that, after the conflict ended in January, a truce was agreed to, a cease-fire, and an agreement was also reached not to undertake any entrenchments or movement of forces along the confrontation lines within the territory of Busovaca municipality.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Thank you. Next document, please?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document D261, D261A for the French version, D261B for the English version.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Brigadier, let me read just a couple of sentences. It is addressed from the Operative Zone of Central Bosnia to the commander of the 3rd Corps of the BH army, Enver Hadzihasanovic. It has no number, but we see the date, 29th of March, 1993: "Protest. In connection with the murder of members of HVO military police. On the 28th of March, 1993, around 2140 hours, at the military police checkpoint in the village of Cajdras, Bernard Kovacevic and Ivan Laus, members of the HVO military police, the Jure Francetic Brigade, were brutally murdered. The murder happened as the above-mentioned persons were on regular duty checking goods and vehicles. The investigation and the information gathered so far indicate that this crime was, indisputably, committed from the immediate vicinity by members of the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina. Several leads suggest that the perpetrators of this act are members of the 7th Muslim Brigade based in Zenica." It is stated that Colonel Tihomir Blaskic drafted this document, but it was not signed. My question, Brigadier, is do you remember this letter or, rather, this event? What do you remember?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN
utterances.text: I remember the event because we were informed about the same by the Jure Francetic Brigade in Zenica. I remember that the commander of the Operative Zone, General Blaskic, addressed a letter to the commander of the 3rd Corps of the BH army, Mr. Enver Hadzihasanovic, in person in order to protest this event.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Specific mention is made of the 7th Muslim Brigade. What can you tell us about that Brigade, especially in connection with this and other similar events that occurred later?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN
utterances.text: At the time, the 7th Muslim Brigade virtually participated in each and every incident that occurred in the Lasva Valley. Also, that brigade, as can be seen from this report, represented a problem for the commander of the 3rd Corps. Furthermore, at the time, we, in the command of the Operative Zone, were not sure whether the 3rd Corps commander really did have control and command over the 7th Muslim Brigade, but because of our own assessments at the time, and in order to initiate certain activities by the 3rd Corps in the direction of the chief of staff of the Bosnian army, so that it might be known who was in command of this brigade, we said, in this report, that we know that this brigade was under the command of the 3rd Corps. Also, the problems that occurred from January until the date of this protest, we recognised this brigade as a threat to the good relations, a threat to relations between the HVO and the BH army. In the last paragraph, the commander of the Operative Zone is asking that the brigade be urgently dissolved, because it harbours confirmed enemies of the Croatian people and that appropriate measures be taken against the command of this brigade. However, as far as I know, no reply was received to this protest.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Brigadier, but was this protest sent to the 3rd Corps?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN
utterances.text: Yes, it was. I'm quite sure of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Next document, please, dated the 14th of April, 1993.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: D262, D262A for the French version, D262B for the English version.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Brigadier, before we read several excerpts from this document, could you please review it, and could you confirm that this is an authentic photocopy of the original document of 14 April, 1993?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: On what basis do you say that?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN
utterances.text: I know Zarko Petrovic, and I know that this information did arrive at the Operative Zone command.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Do you recognise this signature?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: I would like to read some excerpts from this report. This is a report to the Security Information Service in Busovaca. It's dated 14 April, 1993, and it reads: "On April 11, 1993, DL," the initials "DL," "a fighter in a 2nd Battalion contacted us and conveyed to us the information which he obtained through a conversation of Vinko Ljubicic from Zenica regarding alleged army BH intentions towards the Busovaca HVO units. Namely, Ljubicic recounted to DL that, in Zenica, they circulated the news that the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina is prepared to sacrifice between 3.000 and 5.000 people in order to capture the territory of the Busovaca municipality." Brigadier, were such intelligence reports arriving at the Operative Zone command on the eve of the April war in 1993?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN
utterances.text: Yes, these kinds of reports and similar information did arrive, and they kept arriving starting as early as 9 April 1993.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Can we please have the next document?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document D263, 263A for the French version and 263B for the English version.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: First question, Brigadier: Is the document that are you holding in your hand an authentic photocopy of the original document?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN
utterances.text: Yes, this is an authentic photocopy of the original document, because I drafted this document and signed it on behalf of and by authorisation of the commander.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: What is this document? How did it come to be, and what does it consist of?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN
utterances.text: This document was drafted on the basis of the arrest of three officers and a driver from members of the Stjepan Tomasevic Brigade in a situation where three officers, along with the driver, were returning from the frontlines which were held by the Stjepan Tomasevic Brigade towards the army of Republika Srpska, and on that occasion they were captured by the Mujahedins. In order to arrive at the real truth and facts of this matter, the Operative Zone commander tasked me with drafting this command, and it is all itemised here.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: You said they were captured. Were they kept in some kind of prison, detention, or where?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN
utterances.text: To me, it was more like a kidnapping, because these officers were carrying out a task which they were given, and they were taken from there, and we did not know where.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Very well. I would now like to show a videotape of another kidnapping of another officer, and I must say, there is some very graphic scenes, and I would just like to warn any members of the public in the gallery. This is part of D38A. This is an exhibit that was already presented by the Defence, but as this incident occurred on 15 April 1993, on the very eve of the conflict, I would like to reoffer it here.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Brigadier, can you tell the Trial Chamber what is the scene we just saw, what does it represent?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN
utterances.text: The videotape shows a kidnapping of an officer of the Jure Francetic Brigade, who is now Brigadier Zivko Totic.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: And what are the dead bodies there?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN
utterances.text: The dead bodies are the corpses of the escorts of the brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Had you seen this videotape before?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN
utterances.text: I had an opportunity to see this videotape on television as part of an evening newscast.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Can I have the next document distributed please?

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: In your recollection, when did this kidnapping take place?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN
utterances.text: I believe, in my recollection, I believe it was on 15 April 1993.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document D264, 264A for the English version.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Brigadier, can you first review the document, please? And then tell us whether it is an authentic photocopy of the report which arrived at the Central Bosnia Operative Zone command from the forward command post in Vitez on 15th April in the morning?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN
utterances.text: Yes, it is a true copy. I know Zvonimir Maces, it arrived by the packet, it was registered by the communications service, as well as the general service.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: I'm going to read the 4th paragraph. It says, "Our allies were not quiet tonight, either. Blasts could be heard in town until the 0020 hours when there was a lull. Around 2315 hours the bridge by the village of Sarici located in the zone of the Frankopan Brigade was destroyed." And then the second to the last paragraph, "The Muslims have promised to return our flags today between 1200 and 1400 hours from the place they were taken down." I would like to ask you first: What does it mean that blasts could be heard in town? Did that signify war to you, or something else?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN
utterances.text: The blasts, as they were represented here in this document, were a result of the violent actions of the members of the BH army, and intimidating of the population of the town of Travnik.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: And what about the flags?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN
utterances.text: The flags which are mentioned here in the next to the last paragraph were the flags of the Croatian people which were hoisted in certain locations in Travnik, but certain extremists had taken them all down several days before. And after a discussion between the leadership of the Bosnian and Croatian sides in Travnik, the Bosnian Muslim side guaranteed they would be taken back.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: My client has reminded me that Zivko Totic's kidnapping has not been placed in terms of location. Where did it happen?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN
utterances.text: The commander of Jure Francetic Brigade was kidnapped when he was going to his command post, to his headquarters. In other words, when he was going to work. It took place in the vicinity of Zenica, near the command post of Jure Francetic Brigade. I'm not sure if that neighbourhood is called Bikosi. I'm not sure of that. But it is definitely in Zenica. And I would like to also add that this was in the immediate vicinity of this command post.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Thank you. The blasts which were mentioned in Travnik, when you say blasts, does it mean explosives or firearm fire?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN
utterances.text: The word is detonation. It could cover both the explosives and small arms weapons. Mr. Maces did not have formal military training, so he used a word that is more vague.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: The next document is D265, D265A for the English version.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Brigadier, please review this handwritten document. Can you tell me whether this is an authentic photocopy of the special report which arrived in the command post?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN
utterances.text: Yes, it is. It arrived from the Nikola Subic-Zrinjski Brigade, and it was signed by Mato Lastro, I know this person, and it arrived by telefax.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: I'm going to read just the top of it: "On 15 April 1993, at 1505 hours, precisely, in the region of Saracevici, two members of our units were wounded." Do you recall that on the 15th you received a report on the wounding of two HVO members?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN
utterances.text: Yes, I do, and this is a special report, it's not a regular report.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Very well. The next document, please. Do you know by whom these HVO soldiers were wounded?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN
utterances.text: The wounded HVO soldiers were wounded by the members of the BH army, because the area where the incident occurred, in that area the HVO and the BH army forces had been separated since the January conflict.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document is D266, D266A for the English version.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Here is another document which arrived a day before the conflict of 16th April, and I would now like to ask you whether this is an authentic photocopy of the report which arrived to the Central Bosnia Operative Zone by the Stjepan Tomasevic Brigade on 15 April at 1800 hours?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN
utterances.text: Yes, I know Bosu (phoen) Sekic, the brigade duty officer, because I, myself, am from Novi Travnik. The report arrived by telefax and it was received in the brigade headquarters.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: I will read you some excerpts. In the first paragraph it says, "The new political situation in the Travnik municipality is still very complex. The investigation on the missing officers was continued today, but it has not yet produced any results." And then the last paragraph, "All roads in the Novi Travnik municipality continue to be blocked. We would like to note that we managed to get through the food for members of our units located on the defence line against the Chetniks." Could you comment on this, please?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN
utterances.text: The first portion of the report details the results of an investigation which was launched regarding the kidnapping of these missing officers, and it states that no firm facts of this had been produced yet. And then the last part was something that was very important for us at the time which concerned how to continue to supply the members of our units which were on the defence lines against the Chetniks. And in order to resupply these troops, we had to go through the area which was controlled by the BH army. Due to the skills and resourcefulness of the officers of this brigade, they were able to resupply food and other provisions to the units at the frontline without the knowledge of the BH army.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Do you know why the BH army had blocked the roads leading to the defence lines which were held against the Serbs?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN
utterances.text: At that time, and to date, when I reflect on this situation, I, myself, do not know how in a situation like this a partner who was an ally was acting in this way, especially given that this line which was toward the Serbs was the line in front of the Muslim villages.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Very well, Brigadier. I would now like to show the next document drafted by Mr. Blaskic, one day before the break out of the conflict that was on April 15th.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document D267, D267A for the French version, and B for the English version.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Mr. President, this document is longer than one page, but it is a key document regarding these proceedings, on the basis of which a number of actions were carried out which later have been made part of the indictment. So, I would like to read the entire document so that both the Trial Chamber and the public can be fully familiarised with its contents, if you agree with it.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: The date is 15th April 1993, 10.00, and the heading is "Preparatory combat command for the defence of HVO and the town of Vitez from extremists Mujahedin Muslim forces." It is addressed to the commanders of all brigades, 1 through 12, and the commanders of independent units, including the 4th LTRD, military police, and so on. "1: According to reliable data, extremist Muslim forces continue their sabotage terrorist combat activities against members of the HVO, and especially against the command cadre with the goal of frightening the military... and the next word is illegible, "...liquidating the military commanders, bringing in confusion among the HVO ranks..." and, again, the next word is illegible, "... military breakup of the HVO formations and ethnic cleansing of the territory from Croatians." Second paragraph. "Until now, five acts of liquidation of commanders have been carried out. Only once..." and then I can't read the next couple of words, "... out of five attempts, and two attempts at liquidation of the commander of the Central Bosnia Operative Zone and the chief of the HZHB, HVO. Probable intentions of further combat activity will be to occupy the structure of Kuber, and cut it off from Vitez, and then connect with their own forces through Poculica and Kuber with the forces in Vranjska and Kruscica. Occupied TT 661 Svinjarevo, Modenovic (phoen), Gomionica, and connect through Visnjica with the Muslim armed forces, the Mos forces, and then split the territory of the Kiseljak municipality and break up the HVO sources. To the auxiliary forces, they will exhibit activities in the directions already known with the goal of hiding their true intentions and connecting with parts of their forces. By biased information campaign, the forces for psychological propaganda activity will create a space for justification of actions, because their untruths will create a conviction that the Muslims are threatened in the territory under the HVO control. One of the main tasks, of course, is the liquidation of the Operative Zone command, and considering their sabotage activities, its complete destruction for which in the night of 14 April 1993 forces were brought to the facilities of the fire station in Vitez, the school in Kruscica, villages of Nadioci and Ahmici in order to set up a blockade, and to Gornja Rovna and Bezici in order to prevent any assistance for reaching those places; and on 8 April 1993, Krajisnik units were brought to Travnik for interventions. 2. Tasks of our forces. To prevent the politically extreme Muslim forces from carrying out their tasks and be in a state of preparedness for intervention with specific assignments. 2.1: 4th Battalion of the military police. The commander of the 4th Battalion of the military police is directly responsible for the security of the forward command post in Vitez. He must carry out an evaluation of the conditions and reinforce the security in order to prevent any surprises. The Busovaca-Vitez-Travnik road must be free for unobstructed flow of traffic to all persons and military formations, and any setting up of barricades on the part of the Muslim armed forces is to be prevented using the regulations of the military police for regular policing. In the event of a very strong attack by the Muslim extremist forces from the direction of the villages of Nadioci, Ahmici, Sivrino Selo and Pirici, inform me of this, and if the fire is opened directly at you, return it and neutralise the attackers. Pay special attention to the security of the command post and the commander." Next is item 2.2. "The special purpose battalion, Vitezovi, shall act on special task in the event of a breakthrough of the defence line. Its task is to prevent enemy advance, in particular from the direction of Stari Vitez, where the military police of the BH army is located; the civilian Muslim police; and anti-sabotage platoon, the PDV of the BH army, which may act against the command of the Operative Zone. The key task is to carry out the blockade of the above mentioned forces and prevent them from attacking the command. Be prepared to intervene on the basis of these tasks." Next, 2.3. "Tasks of the HVO brigades. Carry out the defence in your given zone of responsibility and prevent the extremist Muslim forces from realising the goal of cleansing of the territory, the genocide against the Croatian people, and full realisation of their objectives. Be prepared to carry out the decisive defence of the territory of the Croatian people. The pull out of forces shall be carried out only after the population has been evacuated and provided for, and upon my approval." And the signature, Colonel Tihomir Blaskic, and signed. Brigadier, will you please look at the last page of this text and tell us whether you recognise the stamp of the Operative Zone and the signature of Colonel Blaskic?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Will you please look at the first page and look at the heading and tell me whether this copy differs from an original preparatory combat order?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN
utterances.text: As far as I can notice, there is no stamp of receipt, which should have been indicated. I don't know why it's missing.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Apart from that, there is no number on it, this document that you have before you; does it differ in any other way from the document compiled in the Operative Zone headquarters on the 15th of April 1993 at 10.00?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN
utterances.text: No. And I confirmed that because I received this document, as can be seen from the last page. My department was called ONO, the abbreviation is indicated.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: What does ONO mean?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN
utterances.text: Operations and training department.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: The interpreters have said that the incoming stamp was missing, but the witness said that the number of the document is missing. For the benefit of the record, let us repeat: Is it correct that in relation to the original document which you received at the time, the only thing that is different is this absence of the number of the document; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: The heading is preparatory combat command; what does that mean in military terminology?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN
utterances.text: In military terminology, preparatory combat command means an assignment to the commanders to whom it is addressed, that in view of the activities of the enemy, they should undertake the appropriate steps and activities within their units in order to prevent the enemy or the opponent realising his intentions.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: In addition to this prepatory combat command, what other command exists?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN
utterances.text: There is the executive combat command when the specific measures and activities are indicated and the deadlines set for the beginning of those activities.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Brigadier, could you tell us what can be inferred from this command? What was the reason for issuing such a command?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN
utterances.text: In addition to a series of incidents that we saw reference to in previous reports, and I shall repeat only some of them, the kidnapping of the commander of the Jure Francetic Brigade and the murder of his escort, the kidnapping of three officers of the Stjepan Tomasevic Brigade and their driver, the wounding of a soldier belonging to the Nikola Subic-Zrinski Brigade at the frontline, the entrenchment of BH army units in the Kula region, explosions and disorderly behaviour in the town of Travnik, and various other incidents that we have confirmed in previous reports. In addition to what was written under item 1, where it says, "According to reliable data, extremists Muslim forces are continuing their sabotage, terrorist combat activities against members of the HVO and especially against the command cadre with the goal of frightening the military," and then there is a word illegible, "liquidating the military commanders."

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: In addition to what we would like to describe as terrorist activities, does this command also mention the probable lines of attack towards the Busovaca-Vitez enclave?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN
utterances.text: Yes. It can be seen from the part of the text which reads: "The probable intentions for further combat activity," then there's a word that is illegible, "to occupy the feature Kuber and cut off," then a word cannot be read, but it is "Busovaca from Vitez, then to connect with their own forces across Poculica and Kuber with forces in Vranska and Kruscica. Also, occupy grid reference 661," which is a key feature for the defence of these localities, "Svinjarevo, Madinovac, Gomionica, and across Visnica, connect with the MRS forces, then split the territory of Kiseljak municipality and break up the HVO forces." So let me repeat: Arrest the commanders, incapacitate the units, and then head towards the ultimate goal that I have just read out.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Tell us, Brigadier, these lines of attack that are referred to in the first part of this command, are they the same lines that you saw from operative reports on the ground?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN
utterances.text: Yes. It is along these axes that the key features are situated, without which the territory of the enclave in the Lasva Valley cannot be defended.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: You were just speaking about the main axes of attack, but this command also mentions supplementary axes of attack. What is the difference between the main and the ancillary lines of attack, and what is the purpose?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN
utterances.text: The bulk of the forces are reserved for the ultimate goal, and that is the main assignment which is indicated here, and that is, to gain control of the indicated territory and to break up HVO forces in that territory. The supporting forces are meant to support the task of the main forces. Those supporting forces can be engaged in blockades, in protecting certain localities, and for intervention purposes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: For the benefit of the record, to make it quite clear, whose main directions of activity are mentioned here? Are they the axes of activity of the BH army or of the HVO?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN
utterances.text: In this item and in this text, the reference is always to the enemy. This can be seen, that the main directions of attack that are referred to are those of the BH army, and the auxiliary forces are also those of the BH army.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Did I understand you correctly, that item 1 of the command describes the expected intentions of the BH army?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN
utterances.text: Yes. That is the rule in all armies.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: The sentence, "To the auxiliary forces, they will exhibit activities in the directions already known with the goal of hiding their true intentions and connecting with parts of their forces," tell me, to the best of your knowledge, where were those auxiliary axes?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN
utterances.text: They were linked to the blocking of communication lines and, thereby, it would be possible for the main forces to carry out their main task unhindered, because HVO forces from neighbouring localities would not be able to come to their assistance, nor would the commander be able to engage forces to help halt the main forces of the opponent.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: According to your assessments at the time, where could the road have been blocked so as to prevent the arrival of units from neighbouring municipalities?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN
utterances.text: As far as we knew, and this was conditioned by the relief itself, the relief of the Lasva Valley, the terrain there, our assessment was that the road could be blocked from Kuber at Kaonik, then in the area of the village of Ahmici, and in the area of the village of Grbavica.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Let us go on to item 2, where it says that certain forces on the night between the 14th and 15th --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Mr. Nobilo, I was hoping that we could finish with this document, but we need to take two breaks. So if you have not finished, let us have a 10- or 15-minute break. We will resume in 10 to 15 minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: We will resume. Please have the accused brought in.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Let us resume, Mr. Nobilo, with the examination of document D267A.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Brigadier, we were discussing the last paragraph of item 1, which is devoted to the intentions of the opponent, that is, the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina. The last paragraph says that certain forces had been brought in in the night of the 14th to the 15th of April, 1993 to the Fire Brigade Centre in Vitez. Will you tell us where it is?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN
utterances.text: The Fire Brigade Centre in Vitez is in the downtown area of Vitez, about 100 metres from the place where the command of the Operative Zone of Central Bosnia was situated.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Am I right in saying that this part of Vitez is called Stari Vitez or Mahala?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: What was situated in the Fire Brigade Centre?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN
utterances.text: The Fire Brigade Centre housed the headquarters of the brigade, the civilian and military police, and these forces that were brought in, that is, parts of anti-sabotage units.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Mr. President, may we approach the relief for the Brigadier to show which were the directions of the attack according to this document?

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Brigadier, could you show us where the Kuber feature is, and where were the forces to be linked up coming from Poculica and Kuber with the forces in Vranska and Kruscica? Where is the main direction of the attack?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN
utterances.text: Mr. President, Your Honours, the Kuber feature is this mountain here (indicating). This is the Kuber feature, the place where forces were to be linked up coming from Poculica and Kuber and those from Vranska and Kruscica. Kuber --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN
utterances.text: This would be the axis.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Can we define that as the main direction of the attack?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN
utterances.text: That is what is stated in the document.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Where were those forces supposed to come from?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN
utterances.text: The forces that were to have crossed Kuber would be coming from Zenica.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Brigadier, can you show us now where, according to you, the auxiliary forces were to block the road, the communications?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN
utterances.text: The auxiliary forces for the execution of this main task of the bulk of the forces were to have blocked the road in three spots, in three places, at Kaonik. This is the intersection of the Vitez-Busovaca-Zenica roads. The other locality where the forces were to block the communication line, that is, near the village of Ahmici. The third spot where the road was to be blocked was at Grbavica village.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: I wish to draw the attention of my colleagues and all parties that the public gallery has no picture on the screen. We're very sorry. We're going to repair the fault, but please continue, Mr. Nobilo. Thank you, Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: For the benefit of the record, all those main directions of attack, as well as the auxiliary attacks intended to block the roads, were to be carried out by which army?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN
utterances.text: Both the main attack and the blocking of the road were to be carried out by the units of the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Let us go on to item 2 of this order, document 267. Item 2 speaks about the tasks of the HVO forces. Tell us, what were the two tasks of the military police?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN
utterances.text: The military police was assigned two tasks, and those are to strengthen the security of the command post building of the Operative Zone command in Vitez, and the second task was to make sure that the communication line remain open.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Which one?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN
utterances.text: The Busovaca-Vitez-Travnik road.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: The Special Purpose Unit Vitezovi, what was their task, according to this order?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN
utterances.text: The Vitezovi Special Purpose Unit was tasked with preventing the advance of the enemy coming from the direction of Stari Vitez, where the military police of the BH army was situated, the civilian Muslim police, and the anti-sabotage platoon of the BH army.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Where were they to attack from Stari Vitez?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN
utterances.text: According to our expectations, they were to gain control of the headquarters of the Operative Zone of Central Bosnia, which was only about 100 metres away. In this way, they would have liquidated the command of the Operative Zone.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: You mean gain control of the Vitez Hotel?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN
utterances.text: Yes. If I may add to that, the main task of the Special Purpose Unit Vitezovi was to block the above-mentioned forces. I underline this, to block those forces.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Brigadier, what about the brigades, the Viteska Brigade, what was its task?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN
utterances.text: We can see from item 3 that the task of the brigades was the same, and it is visible from the title of this order, that it was addressed to all the brigades coming under the Operative Zone of Central Bosnia. The Viteska Brigade did not have any specific tasks separate from others, according to this order. The task was "... to carry out the defence in your zone of responsibility and prevent extremist Muslim forces from affecting open cleansing of the territory and genocide of the Croatian people and the realisation of their goals; to be in a state of readiness to carry out a decisive defence of the territory of the Croatian people, and pull out the forces only after the people have been evacuated and provided for, and only upon my approval."

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Brigadier, you're an officer of the Federation Army, a person with wartime experience. You were present in the headquarters when these orders were written. Tell the Court, according to this order and according to the worst possible interpretation of this order, could it be possible to murder civilians and torch civilian homes?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN
utterances.text: No, under no circumstances.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Next document, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Which document are we talking about? I'm asking the interpreters. I must say that, indeed, the French translation is not very good.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: The next document is D268, D268A for the French version, D268B for the English version.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Mr. President, we have been informed that, grammatically, the translation is not ideal. So if you agree, we would ask the court interpreters to improve upon the translation. The next order, Mr. President, was issued also on the eve of the conflict between the Muslims and Croats, on the 15th of April at 1545. I propose to read it in its entirety, because it is also a key document in these proceedings.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: "Central Bosnia Operational Zone Headquarters." Again, there is no reference number. The date is the 15th of April, 1993. The time is 1545. The name of the order is "Order to Take Action." It is addressed to the brigade commanders listing the names of the brigade and, by hand, Ban Jelacic of Kiseljak is added. Item 1 is entitled: "Enemy. Forces of the 7th Muslim Brigade have intensified their diversionary terrorist activities within the Operational Zone of Central Bosnia and have been acting in a most brutal way (murders, abductions of command personnel, threats to HVO officials, blocking passage on roads, et cetera). These activities have been planned, organised, and promptly executed with the purpose of causing confusion within the HVO units and in order to prepare preconditions for offensive action and for capturing Croatian territory. The 7th Muslim Mountain Brigade, together with the command post in the area of Bilmiste, with the strength of about 1.350 soldiers is organised into three battalions, combat support companies, companies for logistics support, and military police companies. One battalion consisting of troops from Zenica is located in the area of Bilmiste. The 2nd Battalion is located in the area of Han Bila and is composed of soldiers from the Lasva region. The 3rd Battalion is composed of soldiers from Kakanj and Zenica, and a part of this battalion is located in Kakanj, while the other is located in Zenica. The military police units are located in the music school. This brigade enjoys a special status regarding the control and command ideology, supply, and purpose. Interest to join this brigade is particularly strong. Most of the dirty jobs, especially against the HVO, is carried out by this unit. Among the members of this unit are foreigners. The Corps Command has control over this brigade," and then it is added by hand, "but does not take responsibility for their actions. 2) Tasks of our forces. 2.1) In all units within the zone of responsibility of brigades and the 4th Battalion of the military police, combat readiness shall be raised to the highest level, and they shall be prepared to take defensive action. 2.2) EDG diversion and reconnaissance groups composed of 15 soldiers are to be formed in the brigades with the following duties: Take prisoner and destroy, by quick and energetic actions, the diversionary groups of the 7th Brigade, destroy accommodation facilities in the brigade zone of responsibility and, without accepting combat, pull out towards the base. The deadline should be determined by the brigade commander. 2.3) The time limits. Within the zone of responsibility of the 4th Battalion of the military police, an anti-terrorist platoon is to be engaged in combating sabotage terrorist groups of the 7th Muslim Brigade within areas of operation and accommodation of the units (paragraph 1 of this order) with the following task: Take prisoner and destroy, by quick and energetic actions, sabotage terrorist groups of the 7th Muslim Brigade, destroy accommodation facilities, and return to base without accepting combat. The focus of activities should be in the following municipality areas: Busovaca, Zenica, Travnik, Novi Travnik, and Vitez. Time limits and deadlines to be determined by the commander of the 4th Battalion of the military police. 2.4) In the headquarters of all units, teamwork should be ensured and substitutes provided for all members of the staff on a 24-hour basis. 2.5) Monitoring of movements of Muslim forces, sharing information, territory control, and especially control of communication lines shall be increased. 3) Security and protection measures. Security measures of command posts and commanding officers are to be strengthened. All unnecessary movement of officers members of the command shall be banned. Ensure complete protection of the flow of all information between the superior and subordinate headquarters. 4) Information and propaganda activities. In all units, members should be informed on a regular basis about developments within the zone of responsibility and beyond. In order to secure more expeditious and efficient flow of information, achieve full cooperation with the officer for the information and propaganda activities in the headquarters of the Operational Zone for Central Bosnia. 5) Logistics. All materiel and supplies and their consumption are to be placed under strict control, especially fuel consumption, and rationing is to be introduced. 6) Control and command. Secure an uninterrupted system of control and command at all levels. Regular reports shall be sent by 1800 hours in the evening and 600 hours in the morning and extraordinary reports as necessary." It's typed in ten copies, "Commander, Colonel Tihomir Blaskic," signed and stamped. Brigadier, tell us, please, did you see this document on the 15th of April, 1993?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN
utterances.text: Mr. President, Your Honours, this is the document that I, myself, prepared, as can be seen from the initials on page 2 in the bottom left-hand corner. I remember the document, and it was drafted in the command of the Central Bosnia Operative Zone. The document was signed by the Commander, General, or, rather, Colonel at the time, Tihomir Blaskic.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Brigadier, tell me, did that document have a reference number at the time?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN
utterances.text: The document did have a reference number, and it had to have one.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Somebody has added a few things by hand. For example, it says "ONO" at the top of the page. Who wrote that?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN
utterances.text: I did. This is a sign that this document will be handed to me personally.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Somebody also wrote in by hand "Ban Jelacic Kiseljak" in a black pen. Who wrote that?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN
utterances.text: This was written in by General Blaskic himself and in my presence when I brought him the document for his signature.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Somebody, at the end of item 1, also added in black ink and by hand, "But will not assume responsibility for their behaviour." Who wrote that?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN
utterances.text: General Blaskic wrote this at the same time as he entered the name of the Ban Jelacic Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: In every other respect does this photocopy fully correspond to the document you compiled on the 15th of April 1993, somewhere around 1500 hours?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN
utterances.text: Yes, it does.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Tell me, it says here, "Order to take action"; obviously there's a difference between this document and the previous document, which I think was headed "Preparatory combat order." What does it mean?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN
utterances.text: The heading in this document means the putting into practice the activities that need to be taken. It was compiled because through intelligence information we had more complete knowledge than we had at the time of the preparatory order, and also we had more information regarding the general mobilisation in Zenica and the preparation of very strong forces in Zenica which we expected to arrive via Kuber.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Tell me, Brigadier, does this order for action, in the area dealing with anti-terrorist activities, is based in the preparatory command which has been marked D267, and it was issued on the same day but at 1000 hours?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN
utterances.text: Yes, that is obvious from the whole text of this order.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: In item 2.3 mention is made of engaging an AT platoon in the zone of responsibility of the 4th Battalion, it gains terrorist groups; did this anti-terrorist platoon have a special name?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN
utterances.text: The AT platoon, as far as I recall, was known as "Jokery," Jokers.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Please look at 2.5, which says what should be intensified, and special emphasis is placed on roads. Why?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN
utterances.text: 2.5 calls for the monitoring of movement of Muslim forces with special particular attention to communications. When we look at the relief, and it is generally known anyway that in Central Bosnia the forces that have control of the roads, in fact, have control of the entire territory. And for this reason, particular attention is focused on communication lines, especially as the Lasva enclave, its life and destiny depended on those communications.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Will you please observe the last line of item 1 where reference is made to the 7th Muslim Brigade, and where it says that the corps command does have control over this brigade, but distances itself from their actions. According to your knowledge at the time, and later on, was there a clear or unclear chain of command in relation to this brigade?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN
utterances.text: As far as I know, with respect to the 7th Muslim Brigade, the chain of command was not quite clear, at least not to me.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Could it be said that in the case of the 7th Muslim Brigade, the main military principle of unity of command had been violated?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN
utterances.text: According to the knowledge we had, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Next document, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document D269, D269A for the French version, and B for the English version.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Mr. President, this is the third and last combat order which was compiled a day before the combat, in fact, it was also past midnight; and I would also like to read it in its entirety, because I believe it is also very important.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Again, this is the Central Bosnia Operative Zone command, the date is 16 April, time is 0130 hours, and the heading is "Combat command, order to prevent attack activities by the enemy (extremist Muslim forces), and blockade of the wider area of Kruscica Vranska and Donja Vecerska." It is addressed to Mr. Cerkez, the commander of the HVO brigade in Vitez, and to Komertko (phoen), special purpose units. "Item 1: On the basis of the main headquarters of the HVO, and the assessment we have made, we expect an enemy attack in the direction of Kruscica downtown, and Vranjska downtown with a probable objective to, after carrying out the planned terrorist attack, engage in open offensive action against the HVO and destruction of anything Croatian. The enemy will probably use infantry units, and the main forces will be directed against the command and other HVO structures. The task of your forces is to occupy the sector of the defence, block the villages and prevent all entrances and exits from these villages. In the event of an open attack by the Muslims, use small arms weapons, this is what the PN abbreviation stands for, to neutralise them and prevent their movement. The time of preparedness is 0530 hours on 16 April 1993. Combat formation, blockade forces, (observation ambush), and the reception was added in handwriting. Then the search forces and the forces for offensive actions. Number 3. In front of you shall be the forces of the 4th Battalion of the military police; behind you, your forces; to the right of you are going to be the forces of the Nikola Subic-Zrinjski unit; and to the left the forces of the civilian police. Four: The commander of the Vitez HVO Brigade, Mr. M. Cerkez, shall be personally responsible to me for the execution of this task." Five other points of the command conform to earlier specified instructions. And then it is signed by the Commander Tihomir Blaskic, and the document is also stamped. Brigadier, this was drafted at 0130 after midnight on the night of 15th to 16th of April. Were you present when this document was drafted?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN
utterances.text: At this time I was already in my room in the Vitez Hotel and I was not present when this order was drafted.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: When a document is compiled at such a late hour, what was the procedure? Did you have typists on duty or did you have another procedure? How was it done?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN
utterances.text: Outside of the regular hours, which means after 1500 hours, we did not have a typist, a duty typist in the command post. A typist may have stayed normally an hour or two later, but this particular document was compiled in this way: Colonel Tihomir Blaskic may have wrote it by hand and his communications person could have sent it by packet. And you can see that this was typed, then, and then it was taken back to be signed and stamped. And for instance, you can see that the reception desk was added in handwriting.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Do you recognise the signature?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: When you woke up on the 16th of April, did you see this document?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN
utterances.text: Yes. This document, as all the others, were sent to me, and I did see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Did this document have a reference number or registration number?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN
utterances.text: I believe it did have one.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: The heading of this document is "Combat Order, to prevent attacks by the enemy extremist Muslim forces and blockade of the wider area of Kruscica, Vranska and Donja Vecerska." What does a blockade mean, the blockade of the villages to prevent an army from entering and leaving the villages and so on?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN
utterances.text: The control of movement and blockade of villages, in the circumstances under which we were, meant that you would deploy forces before or in front of a Croatian village. They were tasked to stay there, to be armed, not to move about, but to control movements, to end, to prevent that entrance and exit to the village.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Whom?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN
utterances.text: Because they were protecting or standing in front of the Croatian villages, it would be anybody who would attempt to enter there. And at that time, and I don't know, this was midnight, this was the middle of the night, I don't know what information the commander had at that time.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: So, he may have had additional information, so he may have had information that it would be the members of the BH army. However, it also specifies that this, the area, the wider area of Kruscica, Vranska and Donji Vecerska; who lived, predominantly, that is, in those villages?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN
utterances.text: It was absolutely -- it was an absolute Muslim majority, in all these three villages, and as far as the proportions, there would be about 50 to 60 per cent.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Did the forces of the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina exist in these three villages?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN
utterances.text: Yes, they existed in all three villages, and additional forces were brought into that area, which was reflected in a preparatory order. We identified those additional forces which had been brought to these three villages.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: This order, which was issued on 0130 hours on 16 April 1993, was this combat order based on the preparatory order which was issued on 1000, approximately, on the 15th of April?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN
utterances.text: Yes, it was, but it specified this task of blocking these villages. And that is deployment of stationary troops. It does not mean mobilising forces. It was a passive defence with respect to the BH army forces.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: And as an executive combat order, was this order based on the preparatory order which was issued at 1000 at night on the 15th?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN
utterances.text: Yes, you can see that from the point where these points are referred to, this is a document that only specifies the area and the actual time of the these activities.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Let us remain in this area now. Commander Blaskic is telling Commander Cerkez that in front of them is the 4th Battalion, to the right are the Nikola Subic-Zrinjski units, and to the left are the forces of the civilian police; what does that mean?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN
utterances.text: That means that the deployment of forces was such as is reflected here. That means that in the Busovaca area there were, that the Vitez brigade had to its right the Nikola Subic-Zrinjski, to the left the forces of the civilian police.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: But where, exactly?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN
utterances.text: That is the Vitez-Novi Travnik-Busovaca road. Because the military police had their own camp at a location called the Bungalow. This is in the area of the village of Nadioci.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Brigadier, I'll ask you the same question that I asked for the previous two orders, and I want to ask for all three orders: Was implementation of these three orders possible so that all of these orders could be carried out, and yet that attacks on civilians and burning down of their houses and so forth would be possible?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Brigadier, based on your recollection, on 15th April, apart from these three orders, that is one preparatory and two executive combat orders, did Commander Blaskic issue any other oral or written orders which would have changed the meaning of these three orders which we have presented to the Trial Chamber?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN
utterances.text: No, because had he issued any such order, I would have had to know this, given the duty that I was occupying at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: We will now move to the events of the 16th of April. But before we do so, in order to make it quite clear, what was your duty on the 16th of April, that is the first day of hostilities, until the end of April, 1993? In other words, what was your post at the time? What was your duty?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN
utterances.text: I was on duty of the head of the operations training department and the deputy commander of the staff. Starting on 19 April 1993, I was also the Chief of Staff of the Operative Zone command, because Franjo Nakic was not able to reach the command post after 16 April 1993; because on 15th April he went home to sleep, and the communication line at Grbavica was blocked, and there was no other way to reach Vitez. And for that reason, as head of the operations training department, I also worked in the post of the, I worked as the Chief of Staff of the operations zone command.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Can you tell me what those functions are of the Chief of Staff?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN
utterances.text: The Chief of Staff is the key person in any command structure. It is the person who organises the work of the command, has the full insight into all the activities there, because through the Chief of Staff a commander transmits his orders to the subordinate commanders.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Brigadier, is it possible to issue any kind of combat command or receive any kind of relevant military report without Chief of Staff of the command not being aware of it?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN
utterances.text: No, that case is not possible, regardless of how well he performs in his post.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: On the 16th of April the conflict began in the area of Vitez. We're now going back to your recollections, and then later on we shall try and reconstruct events on the basis of documents. What is it that has been imprinted in your memory regarding the 16th of April 1993? Will you tell the Court, please?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN
utterances.text: On the 15th of April 1993, after completing all my duties for the day in the command headquarters, and because night had fallen, and because of the lack of safety for the movement of officers at night-time, because we had learned of various incidents, and my family and home was in Novi Travnik, which is about 15 or maybe 20 kilometres from Vitez; I spent the night in Vitez Hotel where I had my own room, and it was something I had done frequently, before. That night, as far as I can recollect, I went to bed about 2200 hours. During the night, in the morning, as far as I can recollect, it could have been between 0430 and 0500 hours, I was awakened by the sound of explosions, of shells which were falling in the immediate vicinity of the hotel and on the hotel itself. In view of this, I got up, I left the room and went down to the operative officer on duty. I asked him whether he knew what was happening. He couldn't give me an answer. I gave him the assignment that he should contact all commanders that he can communicate with in order to check and see what was happening and where the shells were coming from, the shells which had caused the explosion around the Vitez Hotel. After that I went to the office of the commander, General Blaskic. I knocked on the door and it was locked, because the commander, General Blaskic, used to work and sleep in that office. I woke him up and asked him whether he had heard the explosions. He had already got up, and because of the shells, and the hotel was not a protected building, because the premises where our operation centre was, was directly facing the fire brigade centre, and in the interests of the security of people working in the operation centre, I asked the commander whether I had his permission to relocate that centre to the basement in the hotel where there used to be a cafe bar.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Let us clarify something immediately. Colonel Blaskic, did he always live and sleep in his office, or did he have a house or apartment in Vitez, so only exceptionally on this night he spent the night there?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN
utterances.text: General Blaskic didn't have a house or an apartment in Vitez. All he had was the office where he worked and slept. It is a room of about 4 by 6 metres in size, as far as I can recollect the space where he lived and worked.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Continue, Brigadier. So, you were given permission to relocate to the basement. What happened in the basement?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN
utterances.text: Yes, I was given permission by the commander to organise the relocation of the operation centre from its previous base to the basement. And through the corridors of the hotel, I reached those premises where previously these premises had been used for a cafe called the 55 Cafe. The previous night there was a discotheque there. I tried to open the door, the door was locked. I broke in the door, I entered the room, and the owner of the cafe was sleeping there. I told him what my intentions were, and I asked him to remove and clear up the tables and the empty bottles, everything he would find in a cafe, so that I could locate the operation centre there. This premise, because of its position and the fact that it was dug in underground, it provided greater protection against the shells that were falling around the hotel, even though it was not absolutely safe.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Brigadier, let us stop there for a moment. Please remind Their Honours how many members of the Operative Zone of Central Bosnia command staff had?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN
utterances.text: On the 15th of April 1993, as members of the command, we didn't have any particular assignments given to us by the commander of the Operative Zone. The officers who had completed their work during working hours had left home. As far as I recall, in the command building, that night there were a total of seven officers, me included. There were two officers from Kiseljak, who after the conflict did not go home. There was one officer from Bugojno, one from Kotor Varos and one from Travnik.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: And what was the total number of staff in the command building before the conflict?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN
utterances.text: Before the conflict, when I was talking about the structure and organisation of the Operative Zone command, I said that there was a total of about 25 employees, rather than officers, because we didn't have ranks.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: So, out of the total of 25 staff members, there were 7. You also found the owner of the cafe bar in the basement, because he was sleeping there. Was there any waiter or any hotel staff around; do you remember?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN
utterances.text: The hotel staff, depending on the activities they engaged in, because we also had our meals at the hotel, they still hadn't arrived. The only people in the hotel were only the security officers of the military police, the security for the command building; and that morning I also saw and met the commander of military police, Mr. Vlado Santic.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Do you remember those young men from the military police? Do you know them?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN
utterances.text: After all, I was at the level of command of the Operative Zone, so I didn't really know each and every policeman. So I didn't know the policemen to be able to recollect a particular name, because this security was not provided within the building, but around the building. In the building itself, there was just a reception desk to the Operative Zone command, and when you wanted to see the commander, you would have to report at the reception desk for the policeman to escort you there.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Do you know how many soldiers, how many military policemen, were positioned around the hotel?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN
utterances.text: Because of the situation that we had observed from the previous documents, the sabotage and terrorist activities of the 7th Muslim Brigade, the forces brought into the Fire Brigade Centre, and the knowledge about the intentions of the BH forces in relation to the command post, the commander of the military police had tripled security of the building. Where regularly, under normal conditions, there was one policeman, now there were three and also a certain number of policemen who were resting, because they were working in shifts. Some of them were resting while others were on duty.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: When did the commander enter the basement?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN
utterances.text: After preparing those premises, I asked that the communication system be established immediately, that is, telephone lines. And through the policeman at the reception desk, I asked him to check whether the other officers were awake, and they were, and that he should tell them that they should all come to the basement. After I had reached the basement and cleared it up and set up the premises, I told the commander that the operations centre was ready and that he could come down if he wished to. I think this must have been between 6.30 and 700 hours.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Tell us, Mr. Blaskic and the rest of you from the command got together in the basement about 6.00 or 7.00 in the morning. As far as you can recollect, tell us, in broad lines, what happened? Where was the information coming from?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN
utterances.text: After telephone lines had been established, the commander of the Operative Zone ordered the operative officer on duty to call up all the brigades to see what was happening on the ground. In the command itself, the situation was as follows: Because of the shelling and the situation provoked by the shelling, citizens were calling up the command. There were a large number of calls. People were asking what was happening because, for us, this was a complete, complete surprise.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Could I ask for the usher's assistance to distribute another document?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Perhaps, Mr. Nobilo, we could have a quarter-of-an-hour break before you present that document or, perhaps, if you prefer, distribute the document first, and then we will have a break after that. So, please, distribute the document so as to save time.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: As you say, Your Honour. We can distribute the document during the break, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Yes, fine. We will resume our work at 5.00 p.m.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Let us now resume. Will the accused please be brought in?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Yes. You have the floor.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. As announced, we distributed the document D270, and I don't believe that the Prosecution has a copy. It's a short document. I will read it in its entirety. "Central Bosnia Operative Zone." The reference number is 01-8-240/93. It is issued as an information to the commanders of brigades and independent units. The body of text reads as follows: "This morning, 16th April, 1993, at 0545 hours, an artillery and infantry attack by Muslim forces was launched against Vitez with the aim of destroying the Croatian Defence Council in Vitez and the Central Bosnia Operative Zone command. Inform your commands and troops of these developments and act according to our orders." In my original, the signature is not clear. However, the stamp is clear, as well as the incoming stamp.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
