utterances.text: Brigadier, could you please tell me, first, whether this copy is representative of the document which you saw?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN
utterances.text: Yes. This is a copy that looks like the copy which I received at the command.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: They are talking about artillery attacks. Were you attacked by artillery?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN
utterances.text: The shells which landed around the Hotel Vitez. Those two shells hit the Hotel Vitez directly. The traces of that can still be seen today. One of them hit the wall near the main entrance, and the second rocket, which was launched from a rocket launcher, hit the back entrance which led to the operations centre which was located in the basement where Cafe 55 used to be.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: If you were hit by a rocket and/or by a shell, does that mean that those guns first had to be trained on you and then the coordinates picked up?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN
utterances.text: In order to launch artillery attacks, either from mortars, I don't know what calibre it was, 80, 82, or 120, or from a rocket launcher or from any other artillery piece, for any of this, you need preparations. These preparations take a certain amount of time, because the coordinates need to be established. The hits which were made shows clearly that these coordinates were taken in a very accurate manner, and also it shows that this artillery attack had been prepared in advance.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Very well. Can we have the next document distributed, please?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document D271, D271A for the English version.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: It's another brief document that I'm going to read. This is dated the 16th of April, 1993. The command of the Operative Zone is writing to the commanders of brigades and independent units. It is a report. "We are communicating to you," referring to the number 01-88-240/93, "that the situation is under our control and that we are making all efforts to confine the conflicts which have broken out." Now, Brigadier, have you seen this document before? Do you recognise the signature of Vid Jazbinski?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN
utterances.text: I do recognise it. I have taken part in its compilation. I know Vid Jazbinski, the officer, and the abbreviation that you see here is my own because I used this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Am I right in saying that this document, by reference number, is referring to the previous document?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Can you say what this formulation means, "we are making all efforts to confine or localise the conflict"?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN
utterances.text: As I have said before, this was a report which was meant to inform all the brigades that the town of Vitez had been attacked. After such an information, the commander then tasks the operations duty officer to notify, in writing, so this is an additional report or information which is sent to the brigades, that we have the situation under control and that we are making all efforts to localise these conflicts. That same morning, the commander of the Operative Zone is trying to find ways to stop the hostilities and confrontation with the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina and stop its advance in that area.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: May I have the next report distributed, please?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: The next document is D272, D272A for the English version.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Brigadier, I'm going to read certain excerpts which I think are significant, important, for these proceedings. This is document D272, which was sent from the command of the Operative Zone at 7.00 in the morning on the 15th of April. This is the operations report. "1) On 15 April, 1993 at 1600 hours, we assumed the post of duty officers at the Viteska Brigade. The afternoon and evening hours were quiet, but we received a certain amount of information, both from the brigade members and the civilian population, about the steady movements and regrouping of the BH army forces, especially in Kruscica (the region of Crna Kuca) and around the fire station where the command of the BH army is located. The hours after midnight were quiet and we received no information about any activity. At 0547, two powerful explosions were heard, the directions of which we could not determine, and two minutes later, additional blasts could be heard from the direction of Rovna, immediately followed by explosions and gunfire from all sides. Information started coming in that the small arms fire and mortars of all calibres were being fired against our positions, and we issued an order not to return fire, except when necessary. 2) At that time, the brigade commander was at home, and even before we called him, he was on his way to the command because he had been awakened by the powerful explosions. Along with the two officers on duty in our brigade, there were four more brigade policemen acting as duty officers. When the attack was launched against our units and positions, two of them were sent to the regional police command. Since then, we have lost any trace of them, and they have not returned. As far as we know, they never reached the police either. The citizens are in a state of panic and are constantly requesting any information and advice. We had no contacts with the representatives of civilian authorities and civilian protection because they had not reached their work places, and they are not answering their telephones at home, we assume, because they are in shelters. The majority of officers members of the battalion and brigade command have not yet arrived at the command, and we are completely disorganised here. We are under attack from all sides, and we have no orders or instructions to follow. 3) Since this is a sudden and unexpected attack, some of the soldiers, of whom the majority are young and inexperienced, are panic-stricken. We fear that they will abandon the command out of a desire to make contact with their families, which would reduce us to a situation where we would be left without any security." It was signed by Srecko Petrovic, the operations duty officer at Viteska Brigade. First of all, I want to ask you, Brigadier, whether this is a true copy, an authentic copy, of the report which you received on the 16th of April at 0700 hours?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN
utterances.text: Yes. This is an authentic copy of the original document. It was signed by Srecko Petrovic as the operations duty officer of Viteska Brigade. I know Srecko Petkovic personally. I recognise his signature, and I personally received this report at the Operative Zone command.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Is this report a typical report which you received from the field? Can you tell us something about its contents?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN
utterances.text: The contents, and this can be gleaned from the text, are concerning certain combat operations, the shelling of the town of Vitez, above all, then it addresses a very unsatisfactory situation at the Viteska Brigade, because they were caught by surprise, they did not expect such a powerful attack. And it also refers to the fact that during the night, until the hour which is referred to in the report, everything had been quiet, except, and this is in item 1, certain movements and regrouping of the troops of the BH army were observed in Kruscica in the region of Crna Kuca. It is an area locally known as Crna Kuca, or black house.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: For the most part, were the majority of soldiers of the Viteska Brigade, which was just being established, were they young and inexperienced?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN
utterances.text: Yes, they were young, inexperienced soldiers, and they were providing security at the brigade. Since there was not enough police forces the command of the Viteska Brigade tasked these young, inexperienced soldiers with this duty.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: So, what does the expression young soldier mean?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN
utterances.text: The young soldier actually means that it is a soldier who had not yet undergone military training, full military training and service. The only such institutions at that time would have been the JNA who provided this.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Very well, I have the next document.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document 273, document D273A for the English version.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Brigadier, have you looked at this document? It is another combat report received on the 16th of April 1993, but this one is of 0900 hours, and I'm going to read the pertinent parts. "Attacks by Muslim forces are becoming more and more ferocious and beastial. We have received information that Croatian houses were hit by mortar in Krcevine and Nadioci, and mortar shells have also been landing in the immediate vicinity of our own command. Mortar shells, most probably of 120 millimetre calibre, were most probably fired from the village of Preocica and landed next to the post office building and the building of the Central Bosnia Operative Zone command; whereby, our own command has become a target for Muslim attacks. We have received information that attempts have been made to break through by Muslim infantry forces in the Mlakici region, the middle section of Vitez, Mahala and Kruscica, and the aim is to take control of the territory controlled by our units and destroy our property and personnel. Snipers also have fired on members of our units from several locations in town and suburbs. From the direction of Vjetrenica and Vrhovine the Muslim forces are firing on the Croatian houses in Poculica. The inhabitants of this village have been calling to ask what to do, as their homes have no cellars, and they were in a state of panic and very frightened. The building of the primary school Dubravica, where the Vitezovi are billeting is being fired from Preocica. The Muslim forces have opened heavy artillery fire on our villages and units from Vranjska Rom (phoen) and Besici. At 0815 hours a mortar shell fell on a prefabricated building on the grounds of the football stadium, and some houses in Kamenjace were hit, too. Croatian citizens have been calling from various locations and asked what is going on, what they should do, and whether they should leave their homes." And this is signed by the duty officer at the command, and the signature is not legible. Is this a copy, an authentic copy of the original document you received at 0900 hours on the 16th April 1993?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN
utterances.text: Yes, it is an authentic copy, and what you see in handwriting in the corner is my own signature.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Can you tell me, what are the mortars in the village of Preocica doing there? Can the Serb position be fired upon from the location in the village of Preocica?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN
utterances.text: Given the distance between the village of Preocica and the frontline, that is, the lines where the army of the Republika Srpska was, it is impossible to fire on the positions of the army of the Republika Srpska from the village of Preocica on 16 April 1993. And in order to better understand the situation and the development of the situation, I prepared a map, and I would ask if it could be placed on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Very well, I would just like to ask the usher to please remove the cap from this projector.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Before we move on to the complete reconstruction of the event of that day, what conclusion have you drawn from the fact that large calibre mortars were placed in Preocica from where you could not reach the Serb lines and they were firing in the early morning hours of the 16th of April?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN
utterances.text: That means that the attack activities in that area had been planned by the BH army, because it would not have been possible to organise and use artillery fire without such preparation having taken place much ahead of time.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Let us now go on to this map. Tell us what it represents, please. It can also be seen on the monitor. And we will distribute copies of the map. Will you tell us who made this map, on whose instructions and what it represents?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN
utterances.text: I made the map on the basis of my recollection and the reports I had. It shows the locations of the conflicts and the localities which came under artillery fire on that day. In the key, we see that the circles indicate the areas of conflict, and the arrows show the places which were most heavily shelled on that day.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: By whom?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN
utterances.text: By the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: This map has the number D274.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Brigadier, can you explain to the Court, on the 16th of April 1993, according to your recollections and the reports that we have tendered, where did the conflicts break out?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN
utterances.text: On the 16th of April 1993, the conflict broke out in the following places: Grbavica; Jardol; Krcevine; Stari Vitez; Kruscica; Donja Rovna; Bare, within the municipality of Busovaca; the road near the village of Ahmici; and the Kuber feature, or more specifically the peak called Obla Glava. The following places were exposed to shelling: Poculica, where there were absolutely no HVO units, it was a place with a mixed population of Muslims and Croats; the area of Krcevine; the area of the town of Vitez and the command building; the area of Kamenjace; and the area of Nadioci. Those were the places that on the 16th of April were most heavily shelled. Let me add, Mr. President, Your Honours, the places where only one or two shells fell has not been indicated on this map, but only the places that were exposed to heavy artillery fire.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Next document, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: D275, 275A for the English version.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Brigadier, the next document was sent by the 111th XP Brigade, the date is the 16th of April, 1993. It is addressed to Commander Blaskic, Central Bosnia Operative Zone. The report says, "Chetniks have continued to provoke along the entire defence line." And in the 5th line from the bottom it says, "In Zenica they are continuing with preparations with the intention of overpowering the HVO from Travnik to Tesanj." What does this document tell us? And did other reports reach you outside the Vitez municipality and outside the Viteska Brigade.

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN
utterances.text: The reports from other brigades came irregularly, but at 2400 hours we received one report each from Zepce and Kiseljak. From the first sentence in this report we can see that in the territory of Zepce municipality, Chetniks, or rather the army of Republika Srpska, are provoking and firing along the defence line which was held by the 111th Zepce Brigade, facing Republika Srpska. We see from this line what a delicate position the commander of Central Bosnia is, that is General Blaskic, as well as the difficult positions of all the HVO units in Central Bosnia. The other sentence you referred to tells us that they have certain intelligence information in Zepce about the ultimate goal of the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina in relation to the HVO.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Brigadier, can you confirm that this copy is a faithful copy of the original? If so, tell us on what grounds.

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN
utterances.text: I can confirm that this copy corresponds to the original, because I am familiar with the signature of Ivo Lozancic, and I am also familiar with the stamp of the 111th Brigade from Zepce.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: And you also have the stamp confirming receipt from the Operative Zone?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN
utterances.text: Yes, the communication centre.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: And it has been entered into the register of the Operative Zone. Next document, please. After having told us where the conflicts broke out, let us now try and see what Colonel Blaskic tried to do in that situation. So, please look at the first document that will be shown to you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: I would like to ask the

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: you referred to fundamentalists, and I shall read it. It says, "The fundamentalists," and then in brackets, "BH Bosnia-Herzegovina Muslims"; do you consider all the Muslims of Bosnia-Herzegovina as being fundamentalists, who are constantly advocating peace? Who are those fundamentalists advocating peace?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN
utterances.text: I do not consider the Muslim Bosniaks living in Bosnia-Herzegovina to be fundamentalists, they are certainly not; but within the framework of the Muslim Bosniak people, there were certain groups which by their behaviour and actions demonstrated such characteristics, such tendencies.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: And they were the ones who were advocating peace?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: In any event, that is what the document says. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: The next document has been marked as D276, 276A for the English version. It is a brief one, but I consider it to be important. So, Colonel Blaskic, on the 16th of April 1993, writes: "To the 3rd Corps of the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina in Zenica." And the heading is "Cessation of offensive operations. Demand: This morning your forces launched an attack on the Central Bosnia Operative Zone command. We are surprised and outraged by such an act which came on top of everything else that your members have recently done. We do not want conflict, but this morning we were forced to respond to the attack launched by your members." We are in possession of information that you are moving strong forces from Zenica towards Vitez. If you are really members of the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina, we request that you stop the attack. We are convinced that the Muslim nation is not in favour of conflict with the Croats. Commander of the Central Bosnia Operative Zone, Colonel Tihomir Blaskic," signed and stamped. We received this document from the Prosecutor's office, but regardless of that, Brigadier, do you recognise the signature, and do you recognise the content of this document?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN
utterances.text: I recognise General Blaskic's signature and, in drafting this text, I personally participated.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Is there any difference between this photocopy and the original?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN
utterances.text: No. But I would like to explain the circumstances in which this report was drafted. It was drafted when, on the basis of reports, we learned the large number of places where conflicts had broken out, as can be seen from this map; when General Blaskic realised the size of the effectives engaged by the BH army in these conflicts; also, when we learned and established how fierce the conflict was and the strength of the shelling by the BH army of the town of Vitez itself, and the other localities as indicated on this map; when we realised the nature of the conflict, that this was a conflict between two armies; also, when we learned about all the places that were in jeopardy within the territory of the Lasva Valley.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Did you have a personal assignment in connection with the cease-fire as early as the 16th of April, 1993?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN
utterances.text: Even before we sent this letter, because we felt that some time was required for this letter to reach the command of the 3rd Corps, General Blaskic personally tasked me to contact the command of the 3rd Corps by telephone. I did so on two occasions. I spoke to the operative officer on duty in the command of the 3rd Corps. I introduced myself, giving my name and the position I held at the time, and I said that I was calling on behalf of General Blaskic and conveyed his message: "General Blaskic is requesting that your commanders halt operations, contain the conflict and, in this connection, we are sending a written request which will reach you shortly." In answer to my demand, the reaction was positive, but the situation on the ground did not change. In fact, the conflict intensified.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Next document, please?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document D277, D277A for the English version.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Brigadier, I will read several sentences from this document. It is the Nikola Subic-Zrinjski Brigade sending a report on the 16th of April, 1993 on the situation in the brigade zone of responsibility at 1700 hours to the Central Bosnia Operative Zone. It's a poor copy, but we will do our best. "During the day in the zone of responsibility of the Zrinjski Brigade of Busovaca, combat activities by Muslim extremists continued. At 0530 hours, a fierce infantry attack was launched from the region of Gornja Rovna and Pezici on our positions in the villages of Donja Rovna and Bare. Our units have responded vigorously. There were some combat activities in the region of Kuber and Obla Glava but of lower intensity. During the combat activities, three of our soldiers were killed, two are listed as missing, while we have nine wounded, of whom two seriously." First, this photocopy, is it a faithful copy of the document which the Operative Zone received sometime after 1700 hours on the 16th of April?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN
utterances.text: Yes. It is a faithful copy of the original, and I can confirm it because I remember this report, and I can confirm it on the basis of the stamp of the communications centre and the stamp in the registry of the Operative Zone.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Next document, please?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN
utterances.text: I should just like to add a few words with respect to this document, though it can all be seen from the contents. But it is clear from this document that the attack was not only targeting Vitez, but also Busovaca municipality, that is, the entire enclave. Forces had been mobilised towards the whole enclave.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document D278, D278A for the French version, D278B for the English version.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Brigadier, you have received the text?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Let us wait for a moment for the interpreters to get a copy. It is the Operative Zone of Central Bosnia or, rather, the Commander, Colonel Tihomir Blaskic, on the 16th of April, 1993 at 1530 hours, writes to the General Headquarters of the Croatian Defence Council in Mostar. This is a report on a meeting with Muslim forces. The first sentence says: "Upon the initiative of the British Battalion at the UNPROFOR headquarters in Bila, a meeting was held today with enemy representatives starting at 12.30. Presiding at the meeting was commander of the British Battalion, Major Brian. The HVO representatives were Marko Paskalo and Zoran Pilicic. Representatives of the BH army were Sefkija Djidic and Safet Sivro. Topic of the meeting: Cessation of fire in Vitez. HVO requirements. Offensive operations/actions by Muslim forces in Vitez are to be stopped. Release of the abducted commander of the Jure Francetic Brigade, Mr. Zivko Totic from Zenica; release of abducted members of the HVO brigade headquarters from Novi Travnik. The most important piece of information came from Colonel Stewart, namely, that Commander Totic was alive and may be expected to be released, perhaps, this very day, this being taken care of by UNPROFOR in Zenica. Conclusions reached at the meeting: Cessation of fire, separation of forces, release of prisoners, care for the wounded, UNPROFOR patrols in towns and surrounding villages. Meeting to be held tomorrow on the 17th of April at 900 hours. HVO representatives pointed out that these conclusions would be carried out on our part if the Muslim forces discontinue their offensive actions. Commander Tihomir Blaskic." Were you familiar with this meeting? Do you know the members of the delegation, and do you know the conclusions that were reached at the meeting in Bila?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN
utterances.text: This document is a faithful copy of the original, and I can claim that on the basis of the signatures I recognise, that of General Blaskic, the stamp of the Operative Zone command. It was written by Marko Prskalo as a member of the delegation attending the negotiations, and Vid Jazbinski wrote the document. Why am I underlining this? Because we were surprised. Even the typist couldn't reach the office, so that command officers typed documents themselves so that the correspondence could continue with subordinates and international organisations. I'm familiar with the members of the delegation. Mr. Marko Prskalo was assistant commander for information and political affairs, and Mr. Zoran Pilicic was assistant for personnel, but in this situation, he acted as coordinator with the UNPROFOR forces. The time and place of the meeting is something I'm aware of. I'm familiar with the conclusions reached when the officers returned from that meeting, because I had this document in my files that very day. However, what else does this document tell us? You saw the letter written by General Blaskic to the commander of the 3rd Corps, so this is an initiative to stop the war. I know this because I was constantly with General Blaskic on that day and all other days. Throughout the year, General Blaskic had sought to avoid a conflict between the BH army and the HVO. General Blaskic, even then, after these operations, did not consider the BH army in the full sense of the word "an opponent of the HVO," but rather the forces within the 7th Muslim Brigade, the Mujahedin, and other units of such tendencies, as the enemy of the HVO. Under those circumstances, we sent our delegation to these talks and immediately informed our superior command as to what we had done to achieve a cease-fire with the BH army units.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Could you, Brigadier, tell the Court, the negotiators, Marko Prskalo and Zoran Pilicic, what happened to them on their way back from these talks?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN
utterances.text: Yes. I forgot to mention that. Returning from the negotiations, Marko Prskalo and Zoran Pilicic, outside the entrance to the command building, they were brought there by a warrior of the British battalion of the U.N. Getting out of this vehicle, the warrior could be seen well from Stari Vitez and Mahala and from the Fire Brigade Centre. These two officers or, rather, members of the Operative Zone command, both of them were wounded.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: This was when they were returning from the second meeting, the next day on the 17th?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN
utterances.text: Yes. I've mixed up the days, but I know that they were wounded upon returning from negotiations. I know that they were driven back by the UNPROFOR in a warrior, and this can be confirmed by the UNPROFOR.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: The next document, which was issued immediately after the cease-fire, it is a document issued by Blaskic and addressed to his subordinate units.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document D279, D279A for the French version, D279B for the English version.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: We will end after studying this last document, Mr. Nobilo.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: The document is brief, but it is linked to these negotiations that we have been referring to. The command of the Operative Zone of Central Bosnia, Commander Colonel Blaskic, on the 16th of April, 1993, the first day of the conflict, at 1600 hours, he issued the following order: "Discontinuation of Combat Activities. Order." It was addressed to both the Viteska Brigade and the Nikola Subic-Zrinjski Brigade. "Discontinuation of Combat Activities. Order: Based on the agreement reached between representatives of the Croatian Defence Council and the Muslim forces under the organisation and supervision of UNPROFOR representatives, and in order to carry out the obligations assumed by signing this agreement, as well as to contribute, ourselves, to easing the situation and reducing tensions between units of the HVO and the Muslim forces, I order: 1) All units in your zone of responsibility are to be immediately ordered to discontinue and cease all combat activities against Muslim forces. 2) Inform all members of HVO units under your command with the contents of this order. 3) All problems in connection with the execution of this order are to be regularly reported to me. This order enters into force immediately, and the brigade commander will be accountable to me for its execution." Signed, "Commander, Colonel Tihomir Blaskic." Are you aware of this order? Do you recognise it, and does this copy correspond to the original?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN
utterances.text: The copy does correspond to the original. It was signed by General Blaskic. I recognise the signature. I'm familiar with the content because I typed it, as can be seen by my initials "SM." Zvonko Vukovic actually drafted it.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Was this order carried out? Were hostilities discontinued?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN
utterances.text: We saw that this order was drafted following the agreement reached on the cessation of hostilities. After the members of our delegation, who participated in the talks, returned to the command post and reported to the commander what had happened, the commander issued this order. This order reached our subordinate units. Our units discontinued combat operations, but, as will be seen from the events that followed in the next few days, the BH army used the negotiations as a method and as a means of reaching certain agreements but avoiding respecting them. In this particular case, after the meeting in the UNPROFOR base, the activities of the BH army were, in fact, intensified and were fiercer than prior to the meeting.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Thank you, Brigadier. We have completed our examination for today.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Very well. We will suspend the hearing today. Tomorrow, General, you will come back and we will resume the hearing, as we do regularly on Tuesdays and Thursdays, at 10.00. The hearing is adjourned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: 6.05 p.m., to be reconvened on Tuesday, the 29th day of September, 1998 at 10.00 a.m.
